A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, core theory and experiments. All 32 pages of v1 and 31 pages of v2, including equations, figures and appendices, support comparison despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original neural-network experiments measuring classification accuracy, neural-collapse metrics and information quantities across image and text datasets.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D retain these original experiments and additionally report margin distributions for two more MNIST class pairs.

M1.justification: The analyzed networks, training procedures and representation measures remain unchanged. The NC2 definition moves from Section 4.2 to Section 5.1 with additional explanation, without changing its computation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR10, SST-2, TREC-6 and AG-news. The additional MNIST class-pair visualizations analyze the existing classification setting. Modular arithmetic remains explicitly outside the experimental scope.

E2.justification: No evaluated comparison method or architecture is added or removed. The new discussion of Han et al. (2025) in Appendix A is a literature comparison, without a corresponding empirical comparison.

E3.justification: Training sizes, architectures, initialization settings, optimization budgets and evaluation metrics are retained. The added class-pair plots use the existing MNIST model and the same 16,000-step and 100,000-step checkpoints as Figure 2.

E4.justification: Appendix D.1 and new Figure 5 extend the decision-boundary case study from digits 0 versus 1 to 4 versus 5 and 8 versus 9, checking whether the observed contraction and separation extend beyond the original pair. Existing sensitivity analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: The five-seed averaging practice and existing descriptions of shading as one standard deviation are retained. No additional repeated-run information, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: New Figure 5 supplies additional margin-distribution results showing contraction and improved separation for two MNIST class pairs. Existing experimental curves and reported values are unchanged: Figure 2 still reports 15% test accuracy at 16,000 steps and 88% at 100,000 steps. The changed Figure 3 image only revises the NC2 panel title.

T1.justification: Appendix B.2.3 adds Proposition B.3 and a matrix-determinant-lemma proof that reducing a covariance diagonal entry, under the specified perturbation, decreases the trace and log-determinant IB bounds. The log-determinant bound already appeared within v1's proof. The main theorems and formal assumptions otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and three principal introduction contributions retain their meaning. The conclusion adds a practical claim that monitoring rescaled within-class variance can help determine when continued training will be beneficial, modestly extending the stated implications.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly discusses the looseness of the variance bound versus the Gaussian-tight log-determinant bound. Remark B.6 expands the rationale and applicability of the existing assumptions. Appendix A also explains the claimed consistency with Han et al. through differences between NCC and RNC1. These qualify and elaborate the retained interpretation.

D1.justification: The experimental details move from Appendix B to C with the same architectures, hyperparameters, preprocessing and MI/nHSIC estimation procedures. The code-access address is unchanged. The expanded discussion of theoretical initialization assumptions does not document a changed implementation.

R1.justification: New Appendix A develops a substantive comparison with Han et al. (2025) concerning the central neural-collapse explanation of grokking. Section 2 adds reconstruction-loss work by Schneider and Prabhushankar, while Remark B.6 substantially expands the convergence and initialization literature used to position the assumptions. This extends the research positioning beyond isolated citation edits.

P1.justification: The main narrative is retained, with localized explanatory additions, a new related-work appendix, additional IB-proof subheadings, relocation of the NC2 definition and acknowledgments. V2 also introduces incorrect 'Theorem' references to items still labeled as definitions, remarks or assumptions, including Definition 3.1 and Assumptions B.3–B.5.

P2.justification: The manuscript is comprehensively reformatted into ICLR style, changing typography, title and author placement, heading styles, running headers and figure placement. Figure 1 is redrawn with phase-specific colored connectors, Figure 3 clarifies the NC2 title, and new Figure 5 adds four groups of margin plots. Existing appendix figures are retained as Figures 6–14.

improvement.justification: The added bound analysis and assumption discussion make the existing theory easier to assess, while the additional MNIST class pairs provide limited corroborating evidence. The core experiments and conclusions remain unchanged. These gains outweigh the new cross-reference mistakes, but constitute a modest improvement rather than a substantial strengthening of the paper.
